TFT Set 19 revealed: Free Mythic Chibi, standalone client and True Damage trait

by RiftDaily Admin | Published: Nov 3, 2026 at 19:30 GMT+0000 | TFT, Featured, News

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 23:50
Instaread
  • Follow
  • Follow

  • Follow
  • Follow

TFT Set 19 is bringing a global music-inspired event to Teamfight Tactics, featuring a revamped True Damage trait, a customizable Tour Collection room and free rewards that include 500 Treasure Tokens and a random Mythic Chibi. Riot Games revealed these features in its November 2, 2026 developer announcement, alongside major changes to the game's PC client.

The new standalone TFT client arrives first with Patch 18.6, while Set 19 is scheduled to launch with Patch 19.1 on December 1, 2026. Once the new set begins, players will be able to earn 500 Treasure Tokens by playing one game and a token for a random Mythic Chibi by playing 20 games. Additional compensation is planned for eligible owners of premium cosmetics affected by TFT's Unreal Engine transition.

There is plenty to look forward to, but Riot is keeping the complete champion roster, trait details and several gameplay mechanics under wraps until the full reveal. Here is everything confirmed about the upcoming set, including its release schedule, client improvements, free rewards and the first look at True Damage.

Advertisement

TFT Set 19 release date and patch schedule

TFT Set 19 is scheduled to release on December 1, 2026, with Patch 19.1. That date appears on Riot Games' official patch schedule, although the developer warns that scheduled updates can change. The November 2 announcement confirms that the new set's appreciation missions and in-client experiences begin with Patch 19.1.

The complete rollout involves several updates, with the standalone client arriving before the new set itself.

These are scheduled dates rather than guarantees. Players can check the official TFT patch schedule for changes before each update.

Riot has not announced a confirmed Set 19 PBE start date or exact worldwide launch time. An official PBE date should not be confused with estimates based on previous set releases.

What is the TFT Set 19 music theme?

Riot previously teased a global music event in its 2026 roadmap. The first Set 19 preview now connects that event to recognizable elements of the League of Legends music universe, including True Damage and memorabilia inspired by Riot's virtual music groups.

The idea extends beyond visual presentation. Music will influence trait gameplay through the A-side and B-side system, while the Tour Collection introduces a dedicated space for players to express their preferences and show their progression.

Riot has not yet revealed the complete thematic lineup, every participating music group or an official subtitle for Set 19. Those details are expected to become clearer with the full Set 19 Dev Drop.

The information comes from the Riot Games official TFT Set 19 announcement, which also outlines the next stages of the standalone client rollout.

TFT standalone client: What changes for PC players?

The Teamfight Tactics standalone client launches with TFT Patch 18.6, ahead of Set 19. Instead of relying on the League of Legends client as its main PC interface, TFT will have a dedicated environment designed around its own features, cosmetics, social tools and future events.

Riot says the initial update will require a larger download than usual. It has not provided a specific download size in the November 2 announcement.

Why is TFT moving away from the League client?

Sharing a client with League of Legends made sense when Teamfight Tactics originally launched. Both games shared significant technical infrastructure, and players could access them through one familiar interface.

However, TFT has developed its own identity, with dedicated cosmetics, competitive systems, events and player expectations. Following the move to Unreal Engine, Riot wants greater freedom to build features specifically for TFT without depending on League's existing client structure.

The longer-term plans include improved lobby presentation, more interactive events and previews of Tacticians and Arenas before equipping them. These are development goals, not a promise that every feature will be available on the standalone client's first day.

Can you still switch between League of Legends and TFT?

Yes. Riot confirms that PC players will still be able to move between League of Legends and Teamfight Tactics using a button, even though the games will have separate client experiences.

The separation is primarily about how players access and interact with TFT, rather than removing its connection to the wider Riot ecosystem. Riot's Unreal Engine migration documentation also states that existing Riot Accounts, purchases and currencies remain intact, with RP continuing to be shared between League and TFT on PC.

Players should not assume they need to create a new account or repurchase their cosmetic collections because of the client change.

Leaderboards and improved lobbies in Patch 18.7

While Patch 18.6 establishes the new client, Riot is targeting additional social and quality-of-life improvements for Patch 18.7:

  • Leaderboards: The return of an in-client feature for viewing competitive standings.
  • Easier party creation: Improvements to adding friends to TFT lobbies.
  • Lobby switching: A simpler way to move between solo and party lobbies across different queues.
  • Social usability: A more convenient experience for players who regularly queue with friends.

Riot is also exploring better post-game screens, including ways to share successful compositions and team codes. Improvements to interface scaling on larger PC displays are being investigated following PBE feedback, but no specific patch has been assigned to those changes.

What about TFT Mobile and macOS?

The Patch 18.6 standalone client announcement specifically concerns PC. Riot has not announced a replacement mobile client or new mobile compatibility changes as part of this rollout. TFT Mobile remains a separate application, with its own device requirements.

Mac users face a separate issue related to the Unreal Engine migration. Riot's support documentation lists macOS support as temporarily unavailable on live servers, with PBE-only support introduced during the Set 18 update cycle. The November 2 announcement does not confirm when native macOS live support will return.

Players should consult the official Unreal Engine migration FAQ for platform requirements and compatibility information rather than assuming the Windows client launch resolves existing Mac issues.

TFT Set 19 True Damage trait: A-side and B-side explained

The TFT Set 19 True Damage trait introduces two selectable playstyles based on winning or losing consecutive rounds. The A-side is designed for win streaks, while the B-side allows players to capitalize on loss streaks.

This is one of the first confirmed gameplay mechanics of the music-themed set. Riot describes the feature using the idea of flipping a record, connecting True Damage's musical identity directly to how the trait functions during a match.

The first two columns reflect Riot's announcement. The strategic considerations are preliminary analysis, not confirmed trait effects.

How the A-side and B-side could affect gameplay

Win streaking and loss streaking are already central to TFT economy management. Winning consecutive rounds can provide additional gold while preserving health. Deliberate loss streaking can also generate economy, although it comes at the cost of player health.

True Damage appears intended to create another decision around those familiar strategies. A player with a strong opening board might prefer the A-side, while someone planning a controlled loss streak might find the B-side more suitable.

That does not mean the trait necessarily provides extra gold, changes health loss or automatically switches modes when a streak ends. Riot has not revealed the exact bonuses, activation rules or limitations.

An important unanswered question is how freely players can switch between the two sides. The announcement confirms that switching is part of the trait's design, but does not explain whether changing sides has restrictions or other conditions.

Riot's official gameplay preview demonstrates the two-sided concept and offers an early look at its presentation.

The A-side and B-side distinction should make streak planning an important topic when the complete trait mechanics are published. Until then, any proposed True Damage composition, champion pairing or optimal streak strategy would be speculative.

TFT Set 19 Tour Collection: Customize your music-inspired room

The TFT Set 19 Tour Collection is a customizable in-client room featuring more than 70 personalization options. Arriving with the new set, it lets players create a space inspired by Riot's music universe while displaying their progression throughout Set 19.

Rather than functioning as another battlefield mechanic, the Tour Collection expands the experience surrounding matches. It gives players something visual and personal to develop across the set.

What can players customize?

Riot has confirmed several defining elements of the Tour Collection:

  • More than 70 customization options: Players will have numerous ways to personalize their room.
  • Music-inspired memorabilia: Decorations will reflect bands and artists from Riot's music universe.
  • Progression display: The room is intended to showcase how players progress through Set 19.
  • Personal expression: Players can build a room around their favorite musical identities and characters.

Riot has not detailed the complete decoration catalogue, how every option is unlocked or whether individual customization items will require purchases. Those distinctions matter, especially for players hoping to complete a collection without spending money.

The official Tour Collection preview shows the visual direction of this new experience and how music-themed personalization fits into the standalone client.

The Tour Collection also provides a useful example of why Riot wants a standalone TFT PC client. An evolving, personalized room is easier to build into a dedicated TFT experience than an interface originally designed around League of Legends.

How to get a free Mythic Chibi in TFT Set 19

To get a free Mythic Chibi in TFT Set 19, play 20 games during the new set's appreciation missions. Riot will award a token that can be redeemed through a special banner containing only Mythic Chibis. The resulting Chibi is random, not a guaranteed character of your choice.

Players can also earn 500 Treasure Tokens by playing just one Set 19 game. Both missions are intended for all players, rather than being restricted to owners of premium cosmetics.

Step-by-step guide to the Set 19 appreciation missions

  1. Enter Set 19: Start playing after Patch 19.1 introduces the new set and appreciation missions.
  2. Play your first game: Complete the one-game requirement to earn 500 Treasure Tokens.
  3. Continue playing: Reach the 20-game requirement to qualify for the Mythic Chibi reward token.
  4. Redeem your reward: Use the token on the dedicated Mythic Chibi banner when it becomes available.
  5. Receive a random Mythic Chibi: The reward comes from the eligible selection in that special banner.

Riot has not announced the missions' exact expiration date, every eligible game mode or any additional restrictions. Players should review the final in-client mission descriptions when Patch 19.1 launches.

Can you choose your free Mythic Chibi?

No character selection has been confirmed. The reward is explicitly described as a random Mythic Chibi, obtained through a special banner using the mission token.

Riot also clarified the banner's reward pool. It contains Mythic Chibis only, excluding Unbound Tacticians and Mythic Little Legends. Players therefore know the type of cosmetic they will receive, but not which individual Chibi it will be.

This distinction is important. The appreciation mission does not award a selectable premium cosmetic voucher, and Riot has not announced a complete list of Mythic Chibis available through the banner.

Why is Riot giving away free Mythic Chibis?

The rewards are part of Riot's response to the problems surrounding TFT's Unreal Engine migration. Set 18 introduced significant technical changes, but players also experienced bugs, performance issues, missing features and temporarily unavailable cosmetics.

The appreciation missions are intended to thank the wider player base for its patience, regardless of whether players own expensive cosmetic items.

These rewards were confirmed in the official developer announcement covering Set 19 rewards and compensation.

Additional TFT Set 19 compensation for cosmetic owners

Players who owned qualifying premium TFT cosmetics before Patch 18.7 will receive additional compensation when Patch 19.1 launches. These rewards are separate from the free appreciation missions available to everyone.

Riot is compensating affected collectors because certain cosmetics could not be used during Enchanted Wilds while the team worked on converting them to Unreal Engine.

Who qualifies for the 2 Mythic Medallions?

Players must own a qualifying Mythic Tactician or Mythic Arena before Patch 18.7. Riot has not stated that owning several qualifying items multiplies the two-medallion reward, so players should not assume that compensation stacks for each individual cosmetic.

Who gets the Prestige Chibi compensation?

Players who owned a Prestige Tactician before Patch 18.7 qualify for another Mythic Chibi. Riot has not revealed which Chibi this will be.

This compensation is distinct from the random Mythic Chibi earned through the 20-game appreciation mission. A qualifying Prestige owner can therefore have access to the ownership-based compensation and the general player mission reward.

When will compensation arrive?

Riot says eligible compensation will be delivered automatically when players log in after Patch 19.1 releases. The compensation does not require completing the appreciation missions.

The ownership cutoff matters. Acquiring an eligible cosmetic after Patch 18.7 does not satisfy the announced requirement.

Riot has not published an individual delivery timetable beyond the Patch 19.1 login requirement or confirmed which specific Mythic Chibi Prestige owners will receive.

TFT Patch 18.6 fixes and future Unreal Engine improvements

TFT Patch 18.6 is scheduled to introduce the standalone PC client alongside several gameplay and interface fixes. Riot is targeting problems that have affected the experience since the Unreal Engine migration.

Riot's announced improvements include:

  • Shorter Carousel waiting times: Adjustments intended to bring Carousel pacing closer to earlier sets.
  • Mobile item border fixes: Corrections to item border presentation on mobile devices.
  • In-game chat improvements: Further work on chat functionality and usability.
  • Streamer Mode: The planned return of a missing feature used by content creators.
  • Combat Recap improvements: More timely information and champion names when hovering over champion portraits.
  • Gameplay bug fixes: Additional corrections, with individual changes expected to appear in the official patch notes.

These are announced targets for Patch 18.6. Their inclusion in a developer preview should not be mistaken for confirmation that the changes are already live or that every underlying issue is completely resolved.

How does Patch 18.6 connect to Follow the Fix?

Riot's Official TFT Follow the Fix tracker documents the team's progress on performance, stability, visual clarity, client functionality and cosmetics.

The initiative followed widespread complaints about TFT's transition to Unreal Engine during Set 18. Players reported issues ranging from reduced frame rates and delayed inputs to missing functionality and cosmetics that were not yet usable in the new engine.

Riot has acknowledged those problems and committed to ongoing improvements. Players can read RiftDaily's TFT Follow the Fix and Unreal Engine improvements coverage for a more detailed breakdown of the migration, the problems Riot identified and its repair priorities.

The transition has involved multiple patches rather than one sweeping repair. Our TFT Patch 18.5 notes cover the preceding balance and bug-fix update, providing useful context for the improvements targeted in 18.6.

For players, the main takeaway is that the standalone client and the Unreal Engine recovery effort are related but separate projects. A new client can improve navigation and create room for new features, while performance, gameplay and cosmetic conversion work continues across subsequent updates.

TFT Set 19 champions, traits and upcoming reveals

The full TFT Set 19 champions and traits have not yet been revealed. Riot has confirmed True Damage and teased additional champions and traits, but has deliberately reserved the detailed gameplay breakdown for the upcoming Set 19 Dev Drop.

That means there is not yet an officially complete roster to use for accurate composition guides, champion tier lists or trait breakpoint recommendations.

What should players expect from the full Set 19 reveal?

The biggest missing pieces are the complete champion lineup, trait descriptions, numerical effects and how the set's systems interact during actual matches.

For True Damage specifically, players still need to learn which champions belong to the trait, how its activation levels work and what switching between A-side and B-side changes mechanically.

Once those details become official, it will be possible to build reliable composition recommendations and evaluate how True Damage compares with other Set 19 traits.

Until that information becomes available, players can revisit our TFT Set 18 Enchanted Wilds guide for the current set's mechanics and champions.

Riot's competitive calendar also provides an important event to follow. The TFT Enchanted Wilds Tactician's Crown takes place November 13-15, closing out the Set 18 competitive season. Players following the transition into the next set should keep an eye on official announcements surrounding the tournament and the upcoming Dev Drop.

Frequently asked questions about TFT Set 19

When is TFT Set 19 coming out?

TFT Set 19 is scheduled to launch on December 1, 2026, with Patch 19.1, according to Riot's official TFT patch schedule. The date is subject to change, and an exact global launch time has not been confirmed.

What is the TFT Set 19 theme?

TFT Set 19 features a global music event connected to Riot's music universe. Confirmed elements include the True Damage trait and a music-inspired Tour Collection featuring decorations and memorabilia from Riot's virtual bands.

Will TFT have its own standalone client?

Yes. Riot is introducing a dedicated Teamfight Tactics PC client that separates TFT's interface from the League of Legends client while retaining convenient switching between the two games.

When does the TFT standalone client launch?

The TFT standalone client is scheduled to launch with Patch 18.6 on November 4, 2026. Riot expects a larger download than usual, with additional functionality planned for subsequent patches.

How do you get the free Mythic Chibi in TFT Set 19?

Play 20 Set 19 games after the appreciation missions arrive with Patch 19.1. Completing the requirement grants a token that can be redeemed on a dedicated banner for one random Mythic Chibi.

How do you get 500 Treasure Tokens?

Play one game in Set 19 to complete Riot's introductory appreciation mission and earn 500 Treasure Tokens. The mission is available to all players under the announced reward plan.

Can you choose your free Mythic Chibi?

No choice of individual Chibi has been confirmed. The reward is random and comes from a special banner containing Mythic Chibis only. Unbound Tacticians and Mythic Little Legends are excluded from the banner.

What is the True Damage trait in TFT Set 19?

True Damage is a music-themed trait featuring two selectable approaches to streak management. The A-side supports a win-streak strategy, while the B-side is designed around loss streaking. Exact bonuses and trait breakpoints remain unrevealed.

What is the TFT Tour Collection?

The Tour Collection is a customizable in-client room arriving with Set 19. It includes more than 70 customization options, music-inspired memorabilia and ways to display progression throughout the set.

Will TFT still be connected to League of Legends?

Yes. The games will have separate PC client experiences, but Riot confirms that players can continue switching between League of Legends and TFT. Existing Riot Accounts remain in use, and the Unreal migration documentation confirms that PC RP remains shared.

Who qualifies for TFT compensation rewards?

Players who owned a Mythic Tactician or Arena before Patch 18.7 qualify for two Mythic Medallions. Those who owned a Prestige Tactician before that cutoff qualify for an additional, unannounced Mythic Chibi. Eligible compensation is delivered automatically after logging in following Patch 19.1's release.

What changes are coming in TFT Patch 18.6?

Patch 18.6 is scheduled to introduce the standalone PC client, shorter Carousel waits, mobile item border fixes, improved in-game chat, the return of Streamer Mode, more informative Combat Recaps and additional gameplay bug fixes.

The next chapter of Teamfight Tactics starts with music

TFT Set 19 is shaping up to be more than a routine champion and trait rotation. Riot is combining a music-inspired set with a dedicated PC client, a personalized Tour Collection and a distinctive True Damage mechanic built around win and loss streaks.

For players, the most immediate milestones are the standalone client's arrival in Patch 18.6, the follow-up improvements planned for Patch 18.7 and the Set 19 launch targeted for Patch 19.1. Once the new set begins, the appreciation missions provide straightforward objectives with valuable free rewards, including 500 Treasure Tokens and a random Mythic Chibi.

The biggest gameplay questions remain unanswered. Riot still needs to reveal the complete champion roster, True Damage's numerical mechanics, other traits and the full details of progression through the Tour Collection. Those announcements will determine how the music theme translates into competitive strategy.

For continuing coverage of the full reveal, future patch notes and the first Set 19 composition guides, follow RiftDaily's Teamfight Tactics news and guides. You can also monitor the Official Teamfight Tactics website for upcoming developer announcements and gameplay details.
